decisions.decision: The 104 Fairview Road dump removal hearing was continued two weeks. The administrator will ask the consultant to revise the plan to address DEP comments, including erosion control and riverfront notation.
The applicant for 711 Mass Ave was told to give the commission a written alternatives analysis comparing six and eight units, well before the next meeting. Staff will circulate it to members.
The chair will schedule a workshop on the local wetlands bylaw and its exemptions, on a Wednesday without a meeting.
The 441 Townsend Harbor Road owner is to submit a signed phased work narrative. It will come back as a field change at the next meeting, with a possible lifting of the stop work order.
Staff will send a letter to the 190 Peninsula owners warning of progressive enforcement if there is no response.
At 192 Townsend Harbor Road, the commission will send the town counsel's draft letters before talking with the homeowners.

minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission, meeting by Zoom, heard the Lake Shirley annual management report and acted on several wetlands filings. It approved a field change at 168 West Street, issued negative determinations for 205 Sunset Lane and 2 Gabe's Place, and approved a drain line relocation at 21 Brookview Terrace. Several hearings were continued, including a contested 711 Mass Ave subdivision where the commission asked for a written alternatives analysis. The administrator announced his May retirement.

what_happened.line: The commission continued the 711 Mass Ave four-lot subdivision hearing to the 16th and told the applicant to submit a written alternatives analysis comparing six and eight units.
The commission approved a field change at 168 West Street and approved the drain line notice of intent at 21 Brookview Terrace; vote tallies were not audible.
Negative determinations were issued for 205 Sunset Lane, on condition of updated plans, and for 2 Gabe's Place.
Hearings for 104 Fairview Road, Harper Road and 123 Chase Road were continued; Harper Road is held up by a filing fee the state agency says it has not received.
The conservation administrator announced he will retire on May 31, and personnel is considering part-time administrative help for the office.

why_it_matters: The 711 Mass Ave decision turns on a written comparison of six and eight units, so whether a larger subdivision near wetlands is approved will rest on a document the public may be able to request.
The conservation administrator's retirement and the possible part-time replacement affect how quickly wetlands filings, enforcement orders and trail-grant work are handled in town.
watch_next: The continued 711 Mass Ave hearing on the 16th, and the written alternatives analysis due well before it.
A workshop on the local wetlands bylaw and its exemptions, to be scheduled by the chair on a Wednesday without a meeting.
